asset.title: Cylindrical Map of Venus
asset.credit: NASA / Jet Propulsion Laboratory; Magellan mission
asset.license: Public domain NASA/JPL image; both source pages explicitly identify the image as public domain
asset.license_note: Credit NASA/JPL. No NASA or JPL endorsement is implied. The SolarViews website's separate copyright notice is not the image license; its image caption explicitly says this image is public domain and copyright free.
asset.projection: Simple cylindrical (equirectangular), complete 360-degree longitude by 180-degree latitude map
asset.observations: Composite of the Magellan synthetic-aperture radar image collection, acquired during the 1990–1994 mission at Venus.
asset.colour_interpretation: Simulated orange hues enhance radar structure and are informed by Venera 13 and 14 surface photographs. This is a false-colour radar reconstruction, not an unobstructed visible-light image of Venus or a calibrated surface-colour map.
asset.coverage_limits: Magellan mapped about 98 percent of Venus. Source mosaic data gaps are filled with Pioneer-Venus Orbiter altimetric data or a constant mid-range value. Visible mosaic seams and constant-colour patches are retained; no new terrain is invented by this application.
asset.processing: Downloaded the provider's 3840 × 1920 JPEG thumbnail unchanged. No local cropping, recolouring, resampling, gap filling or generated detail. Commons' source JPEG is a 5120 × 2560 reproduction of the source map.
asset.rendering_guidance: Wrap as an equirectangular map, with north at the top. Keep the radar/false-colour label visible while selected. Lighting, viewing angle and animation rate are illustrative. The rotation marker is an artificial teaching overlay and is not a real surface feature or calibrated longitude marker.
asset.visual_validation: Inspected the downloaded JPEG: full rectangular 2:1 global surface map, stretched polar rows, Maxwell Montes and Aphrodite Terra consistent with source description; no perspective globe, legend or text baked into the map.
